title: Health and Drugs
seo_title: Year 9 Science: Health and Drugs Worksheets (Alcohol Units, Smoking, Medicines)
standard_text: The effects of recreational drugs (including substance misuse) on behaviour, health and life processes; the consequences of imbalances in the diet; the impact of smoking on the human gas exchange system.
meta_desc: Free Year 9 science worksheets on health and drugs: medicines and recreational drugs, alcohol units, depressants and stimulants, smoking, testing medicines and health data. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Drugs change how the body works.
key_sub: Units = strength × volume ÷ 1,000; nicotine addicts and tar causes cancer.
body_html:
How to think about it

A drug is any substance that changes how the body works.

  • Medicines treat illness; recreational drugs such as alcohol, nicotine and caffeine change mood and behaviour.
  • Alcohol is a depressant. Units = strength (%) × volume (ml) ÷ 1,000. Adults should have no more than 14 units a week.
  • Smoke contains nicotine (addictive), tar (causes cancer) and carbon monoxide (reduces oxygen in the blood).
Example

A 250 ml glass of wine at 12%?

12 × 250 ÷ 1,000

Answer: 3 units

Example

Which part of smoke is addictive?

Not tar

Answer: nicotine

Common mistakes

  • Thinking legal drugs are harmless.
  • Thinking alcohol is a stimulant.
  • Thinking antibiotics cure colds.

faq.q: How do you work out units of alcohol?
faq.a: Multiply the strength (%) by the volume in ml and divide by 1,000. For example, 250 ml of 12% wine is 12 × 250 ÷ 1,000 = 3 units.

faq.q: What are the harmful substances in cigarette smoke?
faq.a: Nicotine is addictive, tar causes cancer, and carbon monoxide reduces the oxygen the blood can carry.

faq.q: What is the difference between a stimulant and a depressant?
faq.a: A stimulant such as caffeine speeds up the nervous system. A depressant such as alcohol slows it down.
